    <title>Senior Content Manager (United States) @ Filigran</title><meta name="title" content="Senior Content Manager (United States) @ Filigran" />
    
  
  <meta name="description" content="🌀 THE COMPANY

Filigran, founded in October 2022, stands out in the cybertech ecosystem for its commitment to revolutionizing cyber threat management with a proactive approach. Its mission is to develop innovative open-source solutions designed to anticipate cyber threats, identify security gaps, and strengthen organizational security posture.

Filigran solutions are now trusted by over 6,000 public and private organizations worldwide.


🎯 THE ROLE

We&#39;re looking for a Senior Content Manager to join Filigran Academy — the learning engine behind XTM One, OpenCTI, OpenAEV, and OpenGRC — and take end-to-end ownership of content projects from concept through delivery.

This isn&#39;t a production role or a pedagogy role. It&#39;s both. As a Senior Content Manager at Filigran, you own the full content lifecycle of your assigned projects — from instructional design and SME collaboration through production, quality, and delivery. You are accountable for what learners experience, and you have the autonomy to shape it.

You&#39;ll work alongside other Senior Content Managers, each owning distinct projects end-to-end. Your ownership stays clearly yours, while shared standards and close collaboration with your peers keep the team&#39;s work coherent.


💼 YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own end-to-end content for your assigned projects — from learning design through production, quality review, and LMS delivery

 - Design structured learning paths, courses, and certification programs aligned to learner personas and skill levels (beginner to advanced)

 - Apply instructional design principles (e.g., ADDIE, Bloom&#39;s Taxonomy) to ensure content drives measurable learning outcomes

 - Manage SME relationships across your projects — coordinating with Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to ensure technical accuracy and relevance

 - Maintain production cadence for your projects: scripting, media production, review cycles, and publishing

 - Own quality within your project scope — including pedagogical soundness, tone consistency, and learner feedback integration

 - Contribute to ILT (Instructor-Led Training) development in partnership with the Customer Training Consultant: storyboards, delivery scripts, and alignment with on-demand content

 - Participate in a standing cross-lane harmonization function — shared style guide, tone/quality bar, and template standards — co-owned with peer Senior Content Managers and stewarded by the Director of Content Management

 - Track and report project-level metrics: module releases, completion rates, learner satisfaction, and content validation

 - Leverage AI tools and methodologies to boost content production and workflow efficiency

 - Contribute to team-wide documentation and workflow practices


🤝 WHO YOU&#39;LL WORK WITH

 - You report directly to the Director of Content Management

 - You collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, and Customer Success teams to stay ahead of product changes and translate technical complexity into accessible learning

 - You partner with the Customer Training Consultant to align ILT delivery with on-demand content

 - You work alongside peer Senior Content Managers — each owning distinct projects end-to-end — sharing standards, practices, and team-wide initiatives

 - Cross-project initiatives (shared LMS infrastructure, joint launches, multi-product certification paths) are coordinated through the Director of Content Management

 - You coordinate with Marketing on content launches and Academy positioning


🧬 PROFILE WE&#39;RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3–5 years of experience in instructional design, technical content creation, or a related field in a B2B SaaS environment

 - Demonstrated ability to own content end-to-end — from concept and design through production and delivery — without heavy process scaffolding

 - Strong instructional design foundation: you know how to structure learning for outcomes, not just information transfer

 - Experience managing multimedia production workflows (video, interactive content, visual design)

 - Comfortable engaging directly with subject matter experts and translating technical depth into learner-accessible content

 - Highly organized with strong project management instincts — you manage your own projects and don&#39;t drop threads

 - Proficient in modern content and LMS tooling (e.g., Camtasia, Articulate, Notion, or similar)

 - Comfortable working in a remote, async-first environment

 - Autonomy, ownership, and team spirit

 - Bonus: Experience in cybersecurity, open-source, or technical SaaS environments

 - Bonus: Familiarity with AI-assisted content production workflows


🌱 WHY JOIN FILIGRAN? MORE THAN JUST A JOB.

We’re a fast-growing, global, and fully remote company building open-source cybersecurity solutions, increasingly powered by AI, to help defense teams anticipate threats and act faster.

⭐ What we believe

We believe we do work that matters, uniting defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient &amp; collaborative.

💻 How we work

We do work that matters by combining strong engineering standards with emerging technologies, including AI, to move faster and smarter.

🧭 What guides us

We make our work matter by building a culture grounded in our CORE values of Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility, and Equity. The principles that guide how we make decisions, treat people, and grow together, especially when no one’s watching.


💰 COMPENSATION &amp; BENEFITS

 - Competitive pay + equity - everyone shares in our success

 - Remote-first, flexible, and balanced - work that fits your life

 - Your setup, your choice - pick the gear that works for you

 - Twice-a-year gatherings - we meet in person for regional and global offsites to connect, collaborate, and strengthen our culture beyond the screen


🌍 EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

We enable cybersecurity through inclusion - from code to culture.

At Filigran, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe diversity of our people make our products and our team stronger. We welcome talent of every background, identity, and lived experience, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

What matters here is what you bring, not what you look like, where you’re from, or how you identify.


🚀 READY TO JOIN US?

Apply now and help us build the future of the cybersecurity ecosystem, together." />

            preload.rel = "modulepreload";
            preload.href = "https://cdn.ashbyprd.com/frontend_non_user/9d2556759f97ad8e8df1f95c766ce791002e553a/" + manifest[file].file;
            // Without integrity here SRI is never enforced on the code-split
            // chunks (the bulk of the app), in any browser.
            preload.setAttribute("integrity", manifest[file].integrity);
            preload.setAttribute("crossorigin", "");
            document.head.appendChild(preload);
          });
        }
      });

    <title>Calibration Program Manager @ Mach Industries</title><meta name="title" content="Calibration Program Manager @ Mach Industries" />
    
  
  <meta name="description" content="ABOUT MACH INDUSTRIES

Founded in 2023, Mach Industries is a rapidly growing defense technology company focused on developing next-generation autonomous defense platforms. At the core of our mission is the commitment to delivering scalable, decentralized defense systems that enhance the strategic capabilities of the United States and its allies. With a workforce of approximately 350 employees, we operate with startup agility and ambition.

Our vision is to redefine the future of warfare through cutting-edge manufacturing, innovation at speed, and unwavering focus on national security. We are dedicated to solving the next generation of warfare with lethal systems that deter kinetic conflict and protect global security.


THE ROLE

Mach Industries is seeking a Calibration Program Manager to own the systems that keep measurement tools and equipment accurate, traceable, available, and fit for use across engineering, manufacturing, test, and operations. You will manage the calibration program, equipment lifecycle, service providers, calibration records, and certificate data used to make measurement and product decisions. This role spans Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Test, Quality, Supply Chain, Operations, and external calibration laboratories. The work is hands-on and requires regular engagement with measurement equipment, calibration certificates, inspection processes, production environments, and technical users in Huntington Beach.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the calibration program for measurement tools and equipment used across engineering, manufacturing, test, inspection, and operations.

 - Manage the equipment lifecycle from selection, procurement, registration, and deployment through calibration, repair, retirement, and replacement.

 - Establish calibration intervals, methods, acceptance criteria, traceability requirements, and status controls based on equipment use, risk, stability, and measurement needs.

 - Review calibration certificates and historical results to identify drift, recurring failures, out-of-tolerance trends, overdue equipment, and opportunities to improve calibration intervals.

 - Assess the impact of out-of-tolerance conditions on prior measurements, products, processes, and test results, and coordinate required containment and corrective actions.

 - Define equipment-selection criteria based on intended use, measurement range, accuracy, environment, resolution, reliability, maintainability, and total cost of ownership.

 - Coordinate internal and external calibration activities, including scheduling, vendor qualification, service-level expectations, certificate review, and issue resolution.

 - Maintain accurate calibration records, equipment identification, location, status, ownership, history, and traceability within the applicable quality and asset-management systems.

 - Develop dashboards and reports that communicate calibration health, equipment availability, certificate trends, measurement risk, and improvement priorities to technical and operations leaders.

 - Up to 50% travel


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor&#39;s degree in engineering, metrology, physical science, manufacturing, or equivalent professional experience.

 - Five or more years of experience managing calibration, metrology, measurement systems, inspection equipment, or a related technical program.

 - Knowledge of calibration principles, measurement traceability, uncertainty, equipment suitability, and calibration certificate interpretation.

 - Experience analyzing calibration and equipment-history data to identify drift, recurring failures, out-of-tolerance trends, and measurement risk.

 - Experience selecting, qualifying, maintaining, and controlling measurement tools and equipment based on intended use and technical requirements.

 - Ability to coordinate technical users, external laboratories, suppliers, and cross-functional teams while maintaining accurate records and timely program execution.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience managing calibration programs in aerospace, defense, semiconductor, medical, automotive, or other regulated manufacturing environments.

 - Experience with ISO 17025, AS9100, NIST traceability, A2LA-accredited laboratories, or comparable metrology requirements.

 - Experience with measurement system analysis, Gage R&amp;R, uncertainty budgets, capability analysis, or measurement-method validation.

 - Experience with calibration-management, CMMS, ERP, QMS, asset-management, or laboratory-information systems.

 - Experience building calibration and measurement capability in a startup, high-growth manufacturing, or rapidly changing hardware environment.

Disclosures

This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR).  Please note that any offer for employment may be conditioned on authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export control laws and regulations without sponsorship for an export license.

Mach participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offers may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and training, critical skills, and business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in most offers and are considered part of Mach’s total compensation package. Mach offers benefits such as health insurance, retirement plans, and opportunities for professional development.

Mach is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, Veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law, including those with a criminal history, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws. If you’d like to defend the American way of life, please reach out!

  <meta name="description" content="ABOUT MACH INDUSTRIES

Founded in 2023, Mach Industries is a rapidly growing defense technology company focused on developing next-generation autonomous defense platforms. At the core of our mission is the commitment to delivering scalable, decentralized defense systems that enhance the strategic capabilities of the United States and its allies. With a workforce of approximately 350 employees, we operate with startup agility and ambition.

Our vision is to redefine the future of warfare through cutting-edge manufacturing, innovation at speed, and unwavering focus on national security. We are dedicated to solving the next generation of warfare with lethal systems that deter kinetic conflict and protect global security.


THE ROLE

Mach Industries is seeking a System Reliability Engineer Program Manager to own the end-to-end reliability program for our complex autonomous defense platforms. You will set system reliability targets, drive risk assessments and test strategies, integrate component/sub-assembly inputs from commodity industrialization engineers, and turn field, test, and manufacturing evidence into clear decisions and corrective actions.

This role sits at the intersection of Systems, Design, Avionics, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Test, Quality, and field operations. You will provide technical direction to commodity SIEs, own the reliability data that informs levels of control and critical failure points, and communicate residual risk and recommended mitigations to technical and program leadership. The work is hands-on and requires close engagement with vehicle architectures, hardware, test evidence, manufacturing records, and field data, primarily from our Huntington Beach site.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the system reliability program across architecture, design, integration, qualification, production, and field operation.

 - Define system reliability objectives, allocations, assumptions, and evidence requirements for integrated mechanical, electrical, software-enabled, and propulsion systems.

 - Maintain reliability block diagrams, system FMECA, fault trees, interface-risk assessments, and single-point-failure analyses for platform architectures.

 - Integrate component and sub-assembly reliability assessments from supplier industrialization engineers into system-level risk, readiness, and mitigation decisions.

 - Define targeted qualification, environmental, screening, accelerated-life, and integrated-system tests based on mission risks and failure hypotheses.

 - Lead system-level failure investigations using teardown evidence, test data, manufacturing records, supplier information, and field observations.

 - Establish and maintain failure-reporting, corrective-action, and reliability-growth workflows that connect field and production evidence to design and process changes.

 - Communicate reliability risk, residual risk, confidence, and recommended mitigations to technical and program leadership under schedule pressure.

 - Provide technical direction and systems-level alignment across commodity industrialization engineers responsible for component and sub-assembly reliability.

 - Up to 50% travel


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor&#39;s or master&#39;s degree in systems engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, aerospace engineering, reliability engineering, or equivalent professional experience.

 - Ten or more years of experience in system reliability, hardware reliability, failure analysis, test engineering, or complex electromechanical systems engineering.

 - Demonstrated experience applying reliability block diagrams, FMEA or FMECA, fault-tree analysis, root-cause analysis, or comparable system-reliability methods.

 - Experience allocating system reliability requirements to components and sub-assemblies and integrating their evidence into platform-level decisions.

 - Experience defining targeted tests and mitigations from incomplete reliability data, failure hypotheses, or field evidence.

 - Ability to lead cross-functional technical work, make risk-based decisions, and explain reliability tradeoffs to technical and non-technical audiences.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with aerospace, defense, UAS, propulsion, robotics, autonomous systems, automotive, or other high-consequence hardware.

 - Experience with environmental qualification, accelerated-life testing, reliability demonstration, screening, or integrated-system test campaigns.

 - Familiarity with MIL-STD-810, MIL-STD-1629, MIL-HDBK-217, ARP4761, or comparable reliability and safety standards.

 - Experience with FRACAS, field-failure tracking, closed-loop corrective action, reliability-growth planning, or warranty and recall analysis.

 - Experience coordinating supplier, component, and sub-assembly reliability work across machining, turbomachinery, avionics, PCBA, harnessing, composites, and castings.

 - Experience building reliability programs and technical standards in a startup, high-growth manufacturing, or regulated hardware environment.

Disclosures

This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR).  Please note that any offer for employment may be conditioned on authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export control laws and regulations without sponsorship for an export license.

Mach participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offers may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and training, critical skills, and business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in most offers and are considered part of Mach’s total compensation package. Mach offers benefits such as health insurance, retirement plans, and opportunities for professional development.

Mach is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, Veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law, including those with a criminal history, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws. If you’d like to defend the American way of life, please reach out!

Mach Industries is seeking a System Reliability Engineer Program Manager to own the end-to-end reliability program for our complex autonomous defense platforms. You will set system reliability targets, drive risk assessments and test strategies, integrate component/sub-assembly inputs from commodity industrialization engineers, and turn field, test, and manufacturing evidence into clear decisions and corrective actions.

This role sits at the intersection of Systems, Design, Avionics, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Test, Quality, and field operations. You will provide technical direction to commodity SIEs, own the reliability data that informs levels of control and critical failure points, and communicate residual risk and recommended mitigations to technical and program leadership. The work is hands-on and requires close engagement with vehicle architectures, hardware, test evidence, manufacturing records, and field data, primarily from our Huntington Beach site.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the system reliability program across architecture, design, integration, qualification, production, and field operation.

 - Define system reliability objectives, allocations, assumptions, and evidence requirements for integrated mechanical, electrical, software-enabled, and propulsion systems.

 - Maintain reliability block diagrams, system FMECA, fault trees, interface-risk assessments, and single-point-failure analyses for platform architectures.

 - Integrate component and sub-assembly reliability assessments from supplier industrialization engineers into system-level risk, readiness, and mitigation decisions.

 - Define targeted qualification, environmental, screening, accelerated-life, and integrated-system tests based on mission risks and failure hypotheses.

 - Lead system-level failure investigations using teardown evidence, test data, manufacturing records, supplier information, and field observations.

 - Establish and maintain failure-reporting, corrective-action, and reliability-growth workflows that connect field and production evidence to design and process changes.

 - Communicate reliability risk, residual risk, confidence, and recommended mitigations to technical and program leadership under schedule pressure.

 - Provide technical direction and systems-level alignment across commodity industrialization engineers responsible for component and sub-assembly reliability.

 - Up to 50% travel


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor&#39;s or master&#39;s degree in systems engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, aerospace engineering, reliability engineering, or equivalent professional experience.

 - Ten or more years of experience in system reliability, hardware reliability, failure analysis, test engineering, or complex electromechanical systems engineering.

 - Demonstrated experience applying reliability block diagrams, FMEA or FMECA, fault-tree analysis, root-cause analysis, or comparable system-reliability methods.

 - Experience allocating system reliability requirements to components and sub-assemblies and integrating their evidence into platform-level decisions.

 - Experience defining targeted tests and mitigations from incomplete reliability data, failure hypotheses, or field evidence.

 - Ability to lead cross-functional technical work, make risk-based decisions, and explain reliability tradeoffs to technical and non-technical audiences.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with aerospace, defense, UAS, propulsion, robotics, autonomous systems, automotive, or other high-consequence hardware.

 - Experience with environmental qualification, accelerated-life testing, reliability demonstration, screening, or integrated-system test campaigns.

 - Familiarity with MIL-STD-810, MIL-STD-1629, MIL-HDBK-217, ARP4761, or comparable reliability and safety standards.

 - Experience with FRACAS, field-failure tracking, closed-loop corrective action, reliability-growth planning, or warranty and recall analysis.

 - Experience coordinating supplier, component, and sub-assembly reliability work across machining, turbomachinery, avionics, PCBA, harnessing, composites, and castings.

 - Experience building reliability programs and technical standards in a startup, high-growth manufacturing, or regulated hardware environment.

Disclosures

This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR).  Please note that any offer for employment may be conditioned on authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export control laws and regulations without sponsorship for an export license.

Mach participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

  <meta name="description" content="ABOUT MACH INDUSTRIES

Founded in 2023, Mach Industries is a rapidly growing defense technology company focused on developing next-generation autonomous defense platforms. At the core of our mission is the commitment to delivering scalable, decentralized defense systems that enhance the strategic capabilities of the United States and its allies. With a workforce of approximately 350 employees, we operate with startup agility and ambition.

Our vision is to redefine the future of warfare through cutting-edge manufacturing, innovation at speed, and unwavering focus on national security. We are dedicated to solving the next generation of warfare with lethal systems that deter kinetic conflict and protect global security.


THE ROLE

Mach Industries is seeking a Principal Reliability Supplier Industrialization Engineer  focused on mechanical hardware, composites, and castings to qualify, develop, and scale suppliers that produce reliable components to engineering, manufacturing, and system requirements. You will translate mechanical design intent into capable material, tooling, molding, casting, finishing, inspection, and production processes. This role spans Mechanical Engineering, Structures, Supply Chain, Quality, Manufacturing, Test, and suppliers from early design reviews through prototype, qualification, production, and field support. The work is hands-on and requires regular engagement with composite fabrication, casting processes, inspection data, supplier process development, and hardware qualification.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Lead supplier industrialization for mechanical components, composite structures, castings, and related hardware from design release through production readiness.

 - Support mechanical design reviews by identifying material, tooling, molding, casting, tolerance, inspection, and process risks.

 - Develop commodity FMEAs, supplier qualification requirements, control plans, inspection methods, and acceptance criteria for critical mechanical hardware.

 - Assess supplier capability across composite layup, curing, infusion, molding, casting, heat treatment, finishing, non-destructive inspection, and dimensional inspection.

 - Establish first article requirements, process-validation plans, material-control methods, inspection coverage, and objective evidence for supplier production readiness.

 - Monitor supplier performance using quality, delivery, yield, nonconformance, process-capability, material, and inspection data.

 - Lead root-cause and corrective-action investigations for recurring supplier nonconformances, porosity, delamination, dimensional variation, surface defects, and process escapes.

 - Support obsolescence, redesign, alternate-source, and supplier-transition activities while preserving configuration integrity and production continuity.

 - Feed supplier lessons learned into mechanical design standards, manufacturing methods, inspection strategies, sourcing decisions, and reliability-growth activities.

 - Up to 100% travel


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor&#39;s degree in mechanical engineering, materials engineering, manufacturing engineering, or equivalent professional experience.

 - Ten or more years of experience in supplier industrialization, manufacturing engineering, supplier quality, composites, castings, or related mechanical hardware.

 - Experience with composite fabrication, casting processes, mechanical drawings, GD&amp;T, inspection methods, or material and process controls.

 - Ability to evaluate supplier processes, identify technical risks, and define practical controls for complex mechanical hardware.

 - Ability to communicate clearly with suppliers and cross-functional teams while managing multiple industrialization activities.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with aerospace, defense, propulsion, automotive, or other high-reliability mechanical hardware.

 - Experience with autoclave or out-of-autoclave composites, prepreg, resin infusion, compression molding, or bonded structures.

 - Experience with investment casting, sand casting, precision castings, heat treatment, machining allowances, or casting simulation.

 - Experience with NDI or NDT methods, material certification, special-process qualification, or aerospace and defense quality requirements.

 - Experience supporting prototype-to-production transitions in a startup, high-growth manufacturing, or regulated hardware environment.

 - Experience with FMEA, control plans, first article inspection, process validation, and structured root-cause and corrective-action methods.

Disclosures

This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR).  Please note that any offer for employment may be conditioned on authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export control laws and regulations without sponsorship for an export license.

Mach participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offers may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and training, critical skills, and business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in most offers and are considered part of Mach’s total compensation package. Mach offers benefits such as health insurance, retirement plans, and opportunities for professional development.

 - Support mechanical design reviews by identifying material, tooling, molding, casting, tolerance, inspection, and process risks.

 - Develop commodity FMEAs, supplier qualification requirements, control plans, inspection methods, and acceptance criteria for critical mechanical hardware.

 - Assess supplier capability across composite layup, curing, infusion, molding, casting, heat treatment, finishing, non-destructive inspection, and dimensional inspection.

 - Establish first article requirements, process-validation plans, material-control methods, inspection coverage, and objective evidence for supplier production readiness.

 - Monitor supplier performance using quality, delivery, yield, nonconformance, process-capability, material, and inspection data.

 - Lead root-cause and corrective-action investigations for recurring supplier nonconformances, porosity, delamination, dimensional variation, surface defects, and process escapes.

 - Support obsolescence, redesign, alternate-source, and supplier-transition activities while preserving configuration integrity and production continuity.

 - Feed supplier lessons learned into mechanical design standards, manufacturing methods, inspection strategies, sourcing decisions, and reliability-growth activities.

 - Up to 100% travel


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor&#39;s degree in mechanical engineering, materials engineering, manufacturing engineering, or equivalent professional experience.

 - Ten or more years of experience in supplier industrialization, manufacturing engineering, supplier quality, composites, castings, or related mechanical hardware.

 - Experience with composite fabrication, casting processes, mechanical drawings, GD&amp;T, inspection methods, or material and process controls.

 - Ability to evaluate supplier processes, identify technical risks, and define practical controls for complex mechanical hardware.

 - Ability to communicate clearly with suppliers and cross-functional teams while managing multiple industrialization activities.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with aerospace, defense, propulsion, automotive, or other high-reliability mechanical hardware.

 - Experience with autoclave or out-of-autoclave composites, prepreg, resin infusion, compression molding, or bonded structures.

 - Experience with investment casting, sand casting, precision castings, heat treatment, machining allowances, or casting simulation.

 - Experience with NDI or NDT methods, material certification, special-process qualification, or aerospace and defense quality requirements.

 - Experience supporting prototype-to-production transitions in a startup, high-growth manufacturing, or regulated hardware environment.

 - Experience with FMEA, control plans, first article inspection, process validation, and structured root-cause and corrective-action methods.

Disclosures

This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR).  Please note that any offer for employment may be conditioned on authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export control laws and regulations without sponsorship for an export license.

Mach participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offers may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and training, critical skills, and business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in most offers and are considered part of Mach’s total compensation package. Mach offers benefits such as health insurance, retirement plans, and opportunities for professional development.

Mach is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, Veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law, including those with a criminal history, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws. If you’d like to defend the American way of life, please reach out!

  <meta name="description" content="At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn&#39;t just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.


SENIOR DATA ENGINEER

At Snowflake, we are building the future of the data-driven enterprise. We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer who brings deep technical craft, strong ownership instincts, and the ability to operate across the full data lifecycle — from raw ingestion to production-ready data products.

This is not a role for someone who executes tickets. You will design and build the data infrastructure that powers internal decision-making and external product capabilities, working at the intersection of data engineering, platform thinking, and stakeholder alignment. You will own complex technical decisions, set the bar for data quality and governance, and contribute to a data platform that scales with the business.

The person we are looking for combines engineering rigour with pragmatic judgement — someone who can solve for today while building for the future, and who raises the standard of the teams they work within.

AS A SENIOR DATA ENGINEER AT SNOWFLAKE, YOU WILL:

 - Design, build, and launch production-ready data models and pipelines that scale effectively across the enterprise data lifecycle — from ingestion through transformation, modelling, and consumption

 - Own complex system design decisions end-to-end, evaluating tradeoffs and documenting architectural choices clearly

 - Implement enterprise-grade data governance frameworks and maintain rigorous data quality standards across the platform

 - Develop and optimise data ingestion processes from diverse enterprise sources

 - Align with the Product roadmap to build tools for the data platform and provide feature feedback as an internal customer zero

 - Mature requirements gathering practices and apply Agile methodologies to data product development — including stand ups, sprint planning, reviews, and retrospectives

 - Lead quality assurance efforts by defining testing strategies, identifying risks, and ensuring timely resolution of technical issues

 - Build strong relationships with stakeholders at all levels — from executive to operational — translating ambiguous requirements into well-scoped technical work

 - Proactively adapt to changing business requirements while maintaining solution integrity

OUR IDEAL SENIOR DATA ENGINEER WILL HAVE:

Education &amp; Experience

 - Bachelor&#39;s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field with emphasis on system design, distributed systems, or data warehousing — or equivalent practical experience

 - 5–8 years of hands-on experience building and operating production data pipelines, data models, and platform infrastructure at scale

Technical Skills — Required

 - Expert-level SQL and strong Python skills, with experience in performance tuning, query optimisation, and schema design for large-scale analytical workloads

 - Hands-on experience with Snowflake — including Snowpark, dynamic tables, data sharing, Snowflake Cortex, and cost optimisation techniques

 - Deep expertise in DBT — advanced modelling patterns, testing frameworks, macro authoring, and project-level governance on Snowflake

 - Strong proficiency with Apache Airflow — DAG design, operator customisation, dependency management, and operational best practices

 - Solid understanding of dimensional modelling, data vault, and semantic layer design

Technical Skills — Preferred

 - Experience designing data pipelines and feature engineering workflows for ML model training and inference

 - Exposure to ML tooling ecosystems: MLflow, Feature Stores, vector databases, or LLM serving infrastructure

 - Experience with Snowflake Cortex AI functions or similar LLM API integrations for data enrichment and AI-ready data product development

Technical Skills — Desired

 - Cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, or GCP) — including infrastructure-as-code and cost management

 - Knowledge of streaming ingestion patterns (Kafka, Snowpipe Streaming) and real-time data architecture

 - Familiarity with data contract frameworks and schema registry tooling

Professional Skills

 - Strong system design and architectural reasoning — able to evaluate tradeoffs, explain decisions, and document designs clearly

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting technical recommendations to both engineering and non-technical stakeholders

 - Collaborative problem-solver who actively elevates team practices, not just individual output

 - Self-directed with strong ownership instincts — drives problems to resolution without requiring ongoing prompting

 - Effective at navigating ambiguity and distilling requirements into well-scoped technical work

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

For jobs located in the United States, please visit the job posting on the Snowflake Careers Site for salary and benefits information: careers.snowflake.com http://careers.snowflake.com" />

 - Strong software engineering craft, with special care for developer experience and designing future-proof systems that can evolve along with a rapidly advancing AI landscape.

 - Proficiency with a general-purpose backend language (Python, Rust, C++, Go) and cloud infrastructure (AWS, Kubernetes).

 - BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, or related fields (or equivalent experience)." />

WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT

 - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Perplexity is looking for a deeply technical software engineer to own and evolve our model serving platform, which is responsible for connecting our products and research systems with our inference layers. This mission-critical system gives teams one fast, reliable interface across providers.

You will work at the intersection of distributed systems, AI products, and infrastructure. You will make it dramatically easier for teams across Perplexity to adopt new models, run rigorous experiments, and ship dependable products.

The ideal candidate combines sound technical judgment forged in production systems with active curiosity around the rapidly changing capabilities and failure modes of frontier models.     <title>Strategic Telecom Alliance Manager @ Skydio</title><meta name="title" content="Strategic Telecom Alliance Manager @ Skydio" />
    
  
  <meta name="description" content="Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

Our customers depend on our drones to protect lives and serve their communities.  Every minute of every day, our drones are dispatched to deliver urgently needed data.  Getting that data from the scene to our users depends on having “always on” connectivity.   We&#39;re seeking a technical partnership manager to spearhead collaborations with leading telecom providers, ensuring that our drones can operate wherever our customers need them to.

Location: This is an office-based position that requires 5 days/week onsite at our HQ in San Mateo, CA.


How you&#39;ll make an impact:

 - Develop and implement our strategy for engaging with telecom carriers that both deepens our existing relationships and expands our ecosystem to new partners within the US, North America, and internationally over time.

 - Understand our customers’ needs and negotiate agreements with telecom carriers that serve those needs by enabling network access, providing sufficient data connectivity, and building sustainable business partnerships.

 - Understanding and advocating for our customers in-flight data connectivity by providing simple and easy-to-use connectivity options from the first boot of a drone after it is taken out of the box.

 - Build the business models that support in-flight data access, and monitor usage and costs to validate those models in practice.

 - Set regulatory and telecom carrier certification priorities to ensure that our drones meet certification standards for both regulators and telecom operators.

 - Build field relationships between telecom partners and Skydio’s field team to support major events such as sports games, parades, and other major public gatherings.

 - Assist Skydio mission success in supporting customers and major incidents.

What makes you a good fit:

 - You have a demonstrated track record of translating customer needs into priorities and driving implementation.  This can take many forms, including working with complex implementation projects directly with customers, building products from scratch, or building complex business relationships.

 - You face complexity without fear.  When given a goal and a complex process with lots of moving parts, you can break down the challenge into meaningful steps, and clearly communicate how each of them moves the ball forward – whether the process is a technical program like device certification, or a business process like negotiating a telecom contract

 - You bring strong analytical skills to problems, and once you develop a plan, you can communicate it throughout both Skydio and our partner organizations.  Working with multiple complex projects and overlapping deadlines does not scare you.

 - You have a technical background, demonstrated by either an engineering or technical degree (such as computer science, telecommunications, or a scientific field), and/or work experience managing complex technical requirements.

Nice-to-haves:

 - Prior work at a growth-stage start-up.  Skydio is growing fast enough that you’ll need to know when to use an existing rule book, as well as when you should burn the existing rule book and write a new one.

 - Interest or experience in wireless communication. You don’t need to be an expert with a patent portfolio, but you will need to be familiar with bit rates, quality of service, and large-scale network operations.  If you don’t come in with this knowledge, you just need to demonstrate that you can learn it quickly.

 - Experience with telecommunications.  We are flexible about what this means.  You might have worked directly at a telecom company (AT&amp;T, Verizon, or T-Mobile), or at one of its major suppliers (like Cisco, Nokia, or Ericsson).  What’s important is that you’re interested in carrier network infrastructure and protocols, and how to apply them to new solutions.

 - Familiarity or interest in how to apply new 5G features, such as dynamic slicing, high-reliability and low-latency communications, and radio resource management, for airborne devices.

Compensation Range: The annual base salary range for this position is  $230,000 - $285,000*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends. For some positions the pay may be dependent upon the individual&#39;s regional location.

  <meta property="og:description" content="Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

Our customers depend on our drones to protect lives and serve their communities.  Every minute of every day, our drones are dispatched to deliver urgently needed data.  Getting that data from the scene to our users depends on having “always on” connectivity.   We&#39;re seeking a technical partnership manager to spearhead collaborations with leading telecom providers, ensuring that our drones can operate wherever our customers need them to.

Location: This is an office-based position that requires 5 days/week onsite at our HQ in San Mateo, CA.


How you&#39;ll make an impact:

 - Develop and implement our strategy for engaging with telecom carriers that both deepens our existing relationships and expands our ecosystem to new partners within the US, North America, and internationally over time.

 - Understand our customers’ needs and negotiate agreements with telecom carriers that serve those needs by enabling network access, providing sufficient data connectivity, and building sustainable business partnerships.

 - Understanding and advocating for our customers in-flight data connectivity by providing simple and easy-to-use connectivity options from the first boot of a drone after it is taken out of the box.

 - Build the business models that support in-flight data access, and monitor usage and costs to validate those models in practice.

 - Set regulatory and telecom carrier certification priorities to ensure that our drones meet certification standards for both regulators and telecom operators.

 - Build field relationships between telecom partners and Skydio’s field team to support major events such as sports games, parades, and other major public gatherings.

 - Assist Skydio mission success in supporting customers and major incidents.

What makes you a good fit:

 - You have a demonstrated track record of translating customer needs into priorities and driving implementation.  This can take many forms, including working with complex implementation projects directly with customers, building products from scratch, or building complex business relationships.

 - You face complexity without fear.  When given a goal and a complex process with lots of moving parts, you can break down the challenge into meaningful steps, and clearly communicate how each of them moves the ball forward – whether the process is a technical program like device certification, or a business process like negotiating a telecom contract

 - You bring strong analytical skills to problems, and once you develop a plan, you can communicate it throughout both Skydio and our partner organizations.  Working with multiple complex projects and overlapping deadlines does not scare you.

 - You have a technical background, demonstrated by either an engineering or technical degree (such as computer science, telecommunications, or a scientific field), and/or work experience managing complex technical requirements.

Nice-to-haves:

 - Prior work at a growth-stage start-up.  Skydio is growing fast enough that you’ll need to know when to use an existing rule book, as well as when you should burn the existing rule book and write a new one.

 - Interest or experience in wireless communication. You don’t need to be an expert with a patent portfolio, but you will need to be familiar with bit rates, quality of service, and large-scale network operations.  If you don’t come in with this knowledge, you just need to demonstrate that you can learn it quickly.

 - Experience with telecommunications.  We are flexible about what this means.  You might have worked directly at a telecom company (AT&amp;T, Verizon, or T-Mobile), or at one of its major suppliers (like Cisco, Nokia, or Ericsson).  What’s important is that you’re interested in carrier network infrastructure and protocols, and how to apply them to new solutions.

 - Familiarity or interest in how to apply new 5G features, such as dynamic slicing, high-reliability and low-latency communications, and radio resource management, for airborne devices.

Compensation Range: The annual base salary range for this position is  $230,000 - $285,000*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends. For some positions the pay may be dependent upon the individual&#39;s regional location.

  <meta name="description" content="Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

Our customers depend on our drones to protect lives and serve their communities.  Every minute of every day, our drones are dispatched to deliver urgently needed data.  Getting that data from the scene to our users depends on having “always on” connectivity.   We&#39;re seeking a technical partnership manager to spearhead collaborations with leading telecom providers, ensuring that our drones can operate wherever our customers need them to.

Location: This is an office-based position that requires 5 days/week onsite at our HQ in San Mateo, CA.


How you&#39;ll make an impact:

 - Develop and implement our strategy for engaging with telecom carriers that both deepens our existing relationships and expands our ecosystem to new partners within the US, North America, and internationally over time.

 - Understand our customers’ needs and negotiate agreements with telecom carriers that serve those needs by enabling network access, providing sufficient data connectivity, and building sustainable business partnerships.

 - Understanding and advocating for our customers in-flight data connectivity by providing simple and easy-to-use connectivity options from the first boot of a drone after it is taken out of the box.

 - Build the business models that support in-flight data access, and monitor usage and costs to validate those models in practice.

 - Set regulatory and telecom carrier certification priorities to ensure that our drones meet certification standards for both regulators and telecom operators.

 - Build field relationships between telecom partners and Skydio’s field team to support major events such as sports games, parades, and other major public gatherings.

 - Assist Skydio mission success in supporting customers and major incidents.

What makes you a good fit:

 - You have a demonstrated track record of translating customer needs into priorities and driving implementation.  This can take many forms, including working with complex implementation projects directly with customers, building products from scratch, or building complex business relationships.

 - You face complexity without fear.  When given a goal and a complex process with lots of moving parts, you can break down the challenge into meaningful steps, and clearly communicate how each of them moves the ball forward – whether the process is a technical program like device certification, or a business process like negotiating a telecom contract

 - You bring strong analytical skills to problems, and once you develop a plan, you can communicate it throughout both Skydio and our partner organizations.  Working with multiple complex projects and overlapping deadlines does not scare you.

 - You have a technical background, demonstrated by either an engineering or technical degree (such as computer science, telecommunications, or a scientific field), and/or work experience managing complex technical requirements.

Nice-to-haves:

 - Prior work at a growth-stage start-up.  Skydio is growing fast enough that you’ll need to know when to use an existing rule book, as well as when you should burn the existing rule book and write a new one.

 - Interest or experience in wireless communication. You don’t need to be an expert with a patent portfolio, but you will need to be familiar with bit rates, quality of service, and large-scale network operations.  If you don’t come in with this knowledge, you just need to demonstrate that you can learn it quickly.

 - Experience with telecommunications.  We are flexible about what this means.  You might have worked directly at a telecom company (AT&amp;T, Verizon, or T-Mobile), or at one of its major suppliers (like Cisco, Nokia, or Ericsson).  What’s important is that you’re interested in carrier network infrastructure and protocols, and how to apply them to new solutions.

 - Familiarity or interest in how to apply new 5G features, such as dynamic slicing, high-reliability and low-latency communications, and radio resource management, for airborne devices.

Compensation Range: The annual base salary range for this position is  $230,000 - $285,000*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends. For some positions the pay may be dependent upon the individual&#39;s regional location.

At Skydio we believe that diversity drives innovation. We have created a multidisciplinary environment that embraces the power of diverse perspectives to create elegant solutions for complex problems. We are committed to growing our network of people, programs, and resources to nurture an inclusive culture.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local anti-discrimination laws.

For positions located in the United States of America, Skydio, Inc. uses E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, please visit https://www.e-verify.gov/" />

  <meta name="description" content="Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

Our customers depend on our drones to protect lives and serve their communities.  Every minute of every day, our drones are dispatched to deliver urgently needed data.  Getting that data from the scene to our users depends on having “always on” connectivity.   We&#39;re seeking a technical partnership manager to spearhead collaborations with leading telecom providers, ensuring that our drones can operate wherever our customers need them to.

Location: This is an office-based position that requires 5 days/week onsite at our HQ in San Mateo, CA.


How you&#39;ll make an impact:

 - Develop and implement our strategy for engaging with telecom carriers that both deepens our existing relationships and expands our ecosystem to new partners within the US, North America, and internationally over time.

 - Understand our customers’ needs and negotiate agreements with telecom carriers that serve those needs by enabling network access, providing sufficient data connectivity, and building sustainable business partnerships.

 - Understanding and advocating for our customers in-flight data connectivity by providing simple and easy-to-use connectivity options from the first boot of a drone after it is taken out of the box.

 - Build the business models that support in-flight data access, and monitor usage and costs to validate those models in practice.

 - Set regulatory and telecom carrier certification priorities to ensure that our drones meet certification standards for both regulators and telecom operators.

 - Build field relationships between telecom partners and Skydio’s field team to support major events such as sports games, parades, and other major public gatherings.

 - Assist Skydio mission success in supporting customers and major incidents.

What makes you a good fit:

 - You have a demonstrated track record of translating customer needs into priorities and driving implementation.  This can take many forms, including working with complex implementation projects directly with customers, building products from scratch, or building complex business relationships.

 - You face complexity without fear.  When given a goal and a complex process with lots of moving parts, you can break down the challenge into meaningful steps, and clearly communicate how each of them moves the ball forward – whether the process is a technical program like device certification, or a business process like negotiating a telecom contract

 - You bring strong analytical skills to problems, and once you develop a plan, you can communicate it throughout both Skydio and our partner organizations.  Working with multiple complex projects and overlapping deadlines does not scare you.

 - You have a technical background, demonstrated by either an engineering or technical degree (such as computer science, telecommunications, or a scientific field), and/or work experience managing complex technical requirements.

Nice-to-haves:

 - Prior work at a growth-stage start-up.  Skydio is growing fast enough that you’ll need to know when to use an existing rule book, as well as when you should burn the existing rule book and write a new one.

 - Interest or experience in wireless communication. You don’t need to be an expert with a patent portfolio, but you will need to be familiar with bit rates, quality of service, and large-scale network operations.  If you don’t come in with this knowledge, you just need to demonstrate that you can learn it quickly.

 - Experience with telecommunications.  We are flexible about what this means.  You might have worked directly at a telecom company (AT&amp;T, Verizon, or T-Mobile), or at one of its major suppliers (like Cisco, Nokia, or Ericsson).  What’s important is that you’re interested in carrier network infrastructure and protocols, and how to apply them to new solutions.

 - Familiarity or interest in how to apply new 5G features, such as dynamic slicing, high-reliability and low-latency communications, and radio resource management, for airborne devices.

Compensation Range: The annual base salary range for this position is  $230,000 - $285,000*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends. For some positions the pay may be dependent upon the individual&#39;s regional location.

  <meta property="og:description" content="Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

Our customers depend on our drones to protect lives and serve their communities.  Every minute of every day, our drones are dispatched to deliver urgently needed data.  Getting that data from the scene to our users depends on having “always on” connectivity.   We&#39;re seeking a technical partnership manager to spearhead collaborations with leading telecom providers, ensuring that our drones can operate wherever our customers need them to.

Location: This is an office-based position that requires 5 days/week onsite at our HQ in San Mateo, CA.


How you&#39;ll make an impact:

 - Develop and implement our strategy for engaging with telecom carriers that both deepens our existing relationships and expands our ecosystem to new partners within the US, North America, and internationally over time.

 - Understand our customers’ needs and negotiate agreements with telecom carriers that serve those needs by enabling network access, providing sufficient data connectivity, and building sustainable business partnerships.

 - Understanding and advocating for our customers in-flight data connectivity by providing simple and easy-to-use connectivity options from the first boot of a drone after it is taken out of the box.

 - Build the business models that support in-flight data access, and monitor usage and costs to validate those models in practice.

 - Set regulatory and telecom carrier certification priorities to ensure that our drones meet certification standards for both regulators and telecom operators.

 - Build field relationships between telecom partners and Skydio’s field team to support major events such as sports games, parades, and other major public gatherings.

 - Assist Skydio mission success in supporting customers and major incidents.

What makes you a good fit:

 - You have a demonstrated track record of translating customer needs into priorities and driving implementation.  This can take many forms, including working with complex implementation projects directly with customers, building products from scratch, or building complex business relationships.

 - You face complexity without fear.  When given a goal and a complex process with lots of moving parts, you can break down the challenge into meaningful steps, and clearly communicate how each of them moves the ball forward – whether the process is a technical program like device certification, or a business process like negotiating a telecom contract

 - You bring strong analytical skills to problems, and once you develop a plan, you can communicate it throughout both Skydio and our partner organizations.  Working with multiple complex projects and overlapping deadlines does not scare you.

 - You have a technical background, demonstrated by either an engineering or technical degree (such as computer science, telecommunications, or a scientific field), and/or work experience managing complex technical requirements.

Nice-to-haves:

 - Prior work at a growth-stage start-up.  Skydio is growing fast enough that you’ll need to know when to use an existing rule book, as well as when you should burn the existing rule book and write a new one.

 - Interest or experience in wireless communication. You don’t need to be an expert with a patent portfolio, but you will need to be familiar with bit rates, quality of service, and large-scale network operations.  If you don’t come in with this knowledge, you just need to demonstrate that you can learn it quickly.

 - Experience with telecommunications.  We are flexible about what this means.  You might have worked directly at a telecom company (AT&amp;T, Verizon, or T-Mobile), or at one of its major suppliers (like Cisco, Nokia, or Ericsson).  What’s important is that you’re interested in carrier network infrastructure and protocols, and how to apply them to new solutions.

 - Familiarity or interest in how to apply new 5G features, such as dynamic slicing, high-reliability and low-latency communications, and radio resource management, for airborne devices.

Compensation Range: The annual base salary range for this position is  $230,000 - $285,000*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends. For some positions the pay may be dependent upon the individual&#39;s regional location.

style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Location: This is an office-based position that requires 5 days/week onsite at our HQ in San Mateo, CA.<br /></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>How you'll make an operators.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Build field relationships between telecom partners and Skydio’s field team to support major events such as sports games, parades, and other major public gatherings.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Assist Skydio mission success in supporting customers and major incidents.</p></li></ul><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p When given a goal and a complex process with lots of moving parts, you can break down the challenge into meaningful steps, and clearly communicate how each of them moves the ball forward – whether the process is a technical program like device certification, or a business process like negotiating a telecom contract</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You bring strong analytical skills to problems, and once you develop a plan, you can communicate it throughout both Skydio and our partner organizations. You don’t need to be an expert with a patent portfolio, but you will need to be familiar with bit rates, quality of service, and large-scale network operations.  If you don’t come in with this knowledge, you just need to demonstrate that you can learn it quickly.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Experience with telecommunications. Platform Partnerships builds and grows the relationships that extend OpenAI products through the world’s most important technology platforms. The team works across Product, Engineering, Research, Go-to-Market, Legal, Finance, Marketing, Policy, and Operations to turn partner opportunities into durable product experiences and business outcomes.

We’re hiring a Partner Manager, Monetization to help build, scale, and manage a portfolio of strategic platform and monetization partnerships. You will drive day-to-day strategy and execution, help shape joint roadmaps and commercial opportunities, and translate shared ambition into measurable adoption, usage, revenue, distribution, and product impact.

This is a hands-on individual-contributor role for a skilled generalist who can move between partnership strategy and detailed execution. You will own day-to-day execution across priority relationships, collaborate with senior partnership leads and cross-functional teams, create structure where playbooks are still emerging, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and step into the product, commercial, and operating details required to move work forward.

In this role, you will:

 - Drive day-to-day partnership strategy and execution across priority partners, working closely with Product, Engineering, Research, Go-to-Market, Legal, Finance, Marketing, Policy, and Operations to align roadmaps and deliver outcomes.

 - Own a portfolio of strategic partnerships as businesses: set direction, prioritize opportunities, and drive outcomes aligned with OpenAI’s product and company goals.

 - Contribute to multi-year expansion strategies and joint plans that connect product roadmaps, commercial opportunities, go-to-market motions, and measurable outcomes.

 - Support complex deal execution and commercial negotiations from partner evaluation through product integration, launch, expansion, and renewal.

 - Operate as a cross-functional driver, aligning internal teams and external partners around clear priorities, owners, dependencies, launch readiness, and decisions.

 - Build trusted executive and working-level relationships across both organizations, creating direct communication, shared accountability, and thoughtful pushback when priorities conflict.

 - Establish and run partner operating cadences, including roadmap reviews, business reviews, planning sessions, launch-readiness reviews, issue resolution, and escalation paths.

 - Translate partner needs, technical constraints, customer feedback, and market signals into clear product, ecosystem, and go-to-market recommendations.

 - Define success metrics and communicate performance, risks, tradeoffs, and opportunities through concise, decision-ready materials for internal stakeholders and executives.

 - Resolve blockers with urgency and turn successful first-of-kind work into simple, reusable playbooks and operating models as the portfolio scales.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - 10+ years of experience in business development, product partnerships, product, or related technology roles.

 - Proven experience supporting or leading complex strategic partnerships from 0 to 1 and through scale, including technical or product integrations and measurable commercial, adoption, distribution, or product outcomes.

 - Strong product and technical judgment, with the ability to work credibly with Product and Engineering on APIs, integrations, developer platforms, data flows, agents, or emerging products.

 - Experience supporting or structuring complex commercial and technical agreements while balancing near-term outcomes with long-term strategic value.

 - Strong cross-functional operating skills and experience aligning Product, Engineering, Research, Go-to-Market, Legal, Finance, Marketing, Policy, and Operations to execute complex initiatives.

 - Strong strategic judgment and problem-solving skills, using data and sound judgment to navigate ambiguity, prioritize competing opportunities, and make tradeoffs.

 - Clear communication across executive, technical, commercial, and operational audiences, including through high-quality written plans and decision materials.

 - Ability to build trust, resolve conflict, and manage expectations across functions and company boundaries without relying on formal authority.

 - High agency, low ego, adaptability, and exceptional follow-through; willing to do the detailed work required to move an outcome forward.

 - Experience operating in a high-growth company or a scaled technology platform is preferred.
